passage.text: Last Friday evening, Mr. Brown was on the train home after a long day at work.
passage.reading: ˈlæst ˈfraɪdeɪ ˈiːvnɪŋ, ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn wʌz ɑːn ðə ˈtreɪn ˈhoʊm ˈæftər ə ˈlɔːŋ ˈdeɪ ət ˈwɜːrk.

passage.text: The train was crowded, and he was very tired.
passage.reading: ðə ˈtreɪn wʌz ˈkraʊdɪd, ənd hiː wʌz ˈvɛri ˈtaɪərd.

passage.text: When he stood up at his station, he noticed a black wallet on the seat next to him.
passage.reading: wɛn hiː ˈstʊd ˈʌp ət hɪz ˈsteɪʃən, hiː ˈnoʊtɪst ə ˈblæk ˈwɑːlɪt ɑːn ðə ˈsiːt ˈnɛkst tə hɪm.

passage.text: He picked it up and looked inside.
passage.reading: hiː ˈpɪkt ɪt ˈʌp ənd ˈlʊkt ˌɪnˈsaɪd.

passage.text: There was ten thousand baht in cash and an ID card.
passage.reading: ðɛr wʌz ˈtɛn ˈθaʊzənd ˈbɑːt ɪn ˈkæʃ ənd ən ˌaɪˈdiː ˌkɑːrd.

passage.text: For a moment, Mr. Brown felt tempted.
passage.reading: fər ə ˈmoʊmənt, ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn ˈfɛlt ˈtɛmptɪd.

passage.text: "No one saw me," he thought. "If I kept the money, no one would know."
passage.reading: ˈnoʊ ˌwʌn ˈsɔː miː, hiː ˈθɔːt. ɪf aɪ ˈkɛpt ðə ˈmʌni, ˈnoʊ ˌwʌn wʊd ˈnoʊ.

passage.text: But then he remembered what he always tells his students: honesty is more important than money.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈðɛn hiː rɪˈmɛmbərd ˈwʌt hiː ˈɔːlweɪz ˈtɛlz hɪz ˈstuːdənts: ˈɑːnəsti ɪz ˈmɔːr ɪmˈpɔːrtənt ðən ˈmʌni.

passage.text: So he decided to do the right thing.
passage.reading: soʊ hiː dɪˈsaɪdɪd tə ˈduː ðə ˈraɪt ˈθɪŋ.

passage.text: He took the wallet to the station office, and the staff called the owner.
passage.reading: hiː ˈtʊk ðə ˈwɑːlɪt tə ðə ˈsteɪʃən ˈɔːfɪs, ənd ðə ˈstæf ˈkɔːld ði ˈoʊnər.

passage.text: An hour later, a young woman arrived at the office.
passage.reading: ən ˈaʊər ˈleɪtər, ə ˈjʌŋ ˈwʊmən əˈraɪvd ət ði ˈɔːfɪs.

passage.text: She was a nurse, and the money was her rent for the month.
passage.reading: ʃiː wʌz ə ˈnɜːrs, ənd ðə ˈmʌni wʌz hɜːr ˈrɛnt fər ðə ˈmʌnθ.

passage.text: She was so grateful that she started to cry.
passage.reading: ʃiː wʌz ˈsoʊ ˈɡreɪtfəl ðæt ʃiː ˈstɑːrtɪd tə ˈkraɪ.

passage.text: She wanted to give Mr. Brown a reward, but he said no.
passage.reading: ʃiː ˈwɑːntɪd tə ˈɡɪv ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn ə rɪˈwɔːrd, bʌt hiː ˈsɛd ˈnoʊ.

passage.text: "Just help someone when you can," he told her.
passage.reading: ˈdʒʌst ˈhɛlp ˈsʌmwʌn wɛn juː ˈkæn, hiː ˈtoʊld hɜːr.

passage.text: On Monday, he told his class what happened.
passage.reading: ɑːn ˈmʌndeɪ, hiː ˈtoʊld hɪz ˈklæs ˈwʌt ˈhæpənd.
